title: Material Operator
description:
Job Description:

Job Title: Material Operator

Department: Materials

Your Role on Our Team

At Milwaukee Tool, we are committed to delivering high-quality, innovative solutions to our users. The Material Operator plays a critical role in supporting manufacturing operations by ensuring the safe, accurate, and efficient flow of materials throughout the facility. This position is responsible for receiving, storing, moving, stocking, and shipping materials while maintaining inventory accuracy and supporting uninterrupted production. The role focuses on safety, operational efficiency, and system accuracy in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

You’ll be DISRUPTIVE through these duties and responsibilities

• Consistently demonstrates safety first mindset; follows all safety related processes and procedures, quickly escalates safety related concerns or issues to create a safe work environment for all employees.

• Safely and efficiently operate material handling equipment, including forklifts, high-reach trucks (up to 30 feet), and swing-reach trucks, while meeting productivity, quality, and safety standards.

• Load and unload trailers, containers, and transportation vehicles safely, efficiently, and in compliance with established procedures.

• Maintain work area per 6s facility standards without direction.

• Execute material handling activities based on operational requirements, which may include equipment operation, production line replenishment, container unloading, shipping support, or a combination of warehouse and production support functions.

• Receive inbound shipments, verify materials against receiving documentation, and accurately transfer inventory to designated storage locations in accordance with established procedures.

• Store, stack, and organize raw materials, components, and finished goods to maximize safety, space utilization, and operational efficiency.

• Ensure continuous production flow by timely replenishment of materials and components at assembly and manufacturing workstations.

• Transport finished goods from production areas to designated staging, warehouse, or shipping locations in a safe and efficient manner.

• Return excess, unused, or recovered materials to appropriate inventory locations and complete all required inventory transactions accurately.

• Pick, prepare, stage, load, and ship customer orders while verifying product accuracy, quantities, and shipping destinations.

• Maintain accurate inventory records through timely system transactions and proper documentation of material movements to support inventory integrity and ERP system accuracy.

• Perform daily equipment inspections, maintain required operating and safety logs, and adhere to all company safety, quality, and operational policies and procedures.

• Support warehouse and production team objectives through flexibility, teamwork, and effective communication across departments.

• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance safety, efficiency, accuracy, and overall operational performance.

• Assist with cycle counts, physical inventories, and inventory reconciliation activities as assigned.

• Must be able to work unsupervised and handle multiple tasks.

• Collaborate with production, warehouse, quality, and shipping teams to ensure materials are available and moved efficiently throughout the operation.

• Ability to work overtime with advanced or little notice.

• All other duties as assigned.

The TOOLS you’ll bring with you:

• High School Diploma or GED

• Moderate proficiency to read and communicate in English

• Forklift Certification (Milwaukee will train)

• Attention to detail

• Speed, Agility & Urgency- Demonstrates a proactive sense of urgency by accurately moving, staging, and replenishing materials to support production demands, quickly adapting to changing priorities while maintaining safety and quality standards.

• User Focused, Solution Driven- Maintain a strong attention to detail and accuracy to ensure products meet quality expectations for a positive end user experience.

• Extreme Ownership- Takes full responsibility for individual performance, equipment, inventory accuracy, and operational results by proactively identifying issues, driving solutions, and following through on commitments to support team and business objectives.

• One Team Mentality- Maintain excellent attendance and punctuality, supporting smooth operations and team success

• Disruptive Mindset- Bring positive energy that motivates others while working independently or alongside a team

• Candid- Support a culture of transparency and accountability across the production floor through honest, direct feedback

• Relentless Improvement- The initiative to identify opportunities for process improvement, raising the standard for yourself and your team.

Working Conditions:

• The employee may be required to frequently lift, carry, push or pull up to 35 pounds

• Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus

• Prolonged standing and/or walking for up to 12 hours per shift

• Ability to work in a non-climate-controlled environment

• Frequent bending, crouching, twisting, reaching

• Comfortable working at heights up to 30 feet using lifts, such as man-ups, to access inventory

• Employees are required to wear the proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) as intended

Milwaukee Tool is an equal opportunity employer.

title: Design Researcher 2
description:
Job Description:

About TTI

TTI is a world-class leader in design, manufacturing and marketing of power tools and accessories, outdoor product equipment and floor care for consumers, professional and industrial users in the home improvement, repair and construction industries. Our unrelenting strategic focus on powerful brands, innovative products, operational excellence and exceptional people drives our culture. This focus and drive provides TTI with a powerful platform for sustainable leadership and strong growth.

Our brands and products are recognized worldwide for their deep heritage, superior quality, outstanding performance and compelling innovation. Our products include professional power tools and accessories, outdoor power equipment and floor care. Our brands include Milwaukee®, AEG®, Ryobi®, Homelite®, Oreck®, Hoover®, Dirt Devil® and Vax®.

About the Advanced Concepts Team

Advanced Concepts is an early innovation R&D group comprised of researchers, engineers, and designers within the Consumer Power Tools for the RYOBI and RIDGID brands. We work with teams throughout the company including engineering, industrial design, analytical, and product management to deliver both exploratory and evaluative user research findings that drive concept development and prototype evaluation. We are a very hands-on group that thrives on learning throughout our diverse projects and apply our skillsets to create new and innovative products that meet our users' needs.

Job Summary

We are looking for a Design Researcher to join our Advanced Concepts team at TTI within the Consumer Power Tools Group, supporting the RYOBI and RIDGID brands in Anderson, South Carolina. The Design Researcher will join the Advanced Concepts team to explore our users' needs, pain points, and contexts delivering actionable insights to the Product Development team. The primary research methodology of this Design Research role is in-field qualitative research, with supplemental quantitative and online research.

This role will be onsite at our Anderson, SC location.

Responsibilities

• Lead scoping and discovery research to understand consumer needs, behaviors, and pain points, including in-home and in-field ethnography, in-depth interviews, and contextual inquiry in the real environments where people live and work

• Synthesize research into clear, compelling insights and bring them to life through storytelling and sessions that build genuine consumer empathy across engineering, design, and product teams

• Partner with concept teams to translate insights into opportunity spaces, facilitating work sessions that move from what consumers need to what we could build

• Evaluate and downselect concepts from the consumer lens, helping the team focus on ideas that solve real problems

• Take concepts into field with real users to evaluate early prototypes, iterate based on honest feedback, and validate that the solution actually works

• Synthesize and document learnings at the end of each project and hand off insights to engineering and product development teams to inform what gets built

• Contribute to building a network of engaged consumers who can participate in ongoing research, co-creation, and feedback sessions over time

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Consumer Insights, Communications, Psychology, Sociology, Industrial Design, or a related field. What matters is how you think about people and how you tell their story, not your major.

Master's degree welcome but not required.

• Qualitative research skills: in-home / in-field ethnography, in-depth interviews (IDIs), contextual inquiry, and prototype evaluation

• Analytical: comfort analyzing qualitative and quantitative data and finding the insight that matters

• Category thinking: understands consumer behavior and can identify unmet needs, gaps, and opportunity spaces

• Synthesis: turns complex, messy findings into clear and actionable direction

• Ability to translate consumer needs into language engineers and product teams can act on

• Strong work ethic

• Ability to work within a multi-disciplinary team effectively

• Disposition to thrive in a fast-paced environment with responsibility for multiple projects at once

• 25-35% overnight domestic travel

Mid-Level: 3-5 years of experience with demonstrated involvement in front-end innovation, consumer insights, or new product development

We Value

• Researchers who are genuinely curious about why consumers behave the way they do

• Innovation mindset: comfortable with ambiguity and able to connect insights to opportunity spaces

• Maker mindset: excited to jump into a new project and not afraid to get their hands dirty

• Comfort in field environments: people's homes, garages, and job sites

• Experience with durable goods, physical products, or hands-on consumer categories is a plus

• Collaborative contributors who bring outside experience and interests to brainstorms

• Cross-functional communicators who can bridge consumer insights and engineering teams

Benefits

We offer competitive wages and a comprehensive benefits package: tuition assistance, 401(k), medical/dental/vision coverage, vacation and holidays.

TTI is a world-class leader in design, manufacturing and marketing of power tools and accessories, outdoor product equipment, and floor care products. Our consumers range from professional and industrial users in the home improvement, repair, and construction industries to homeowners & DIY enthusiasts. Our unrelenting strategic focus on powerful brands, innovative products, operational excellence, and exceptional people drives our culture. This focus and drive provide TTI with a powerful platform for sustainable leadership and strong growth.

Our brands and products are recognized worldwide for their deep heritage, superior quality, outstanding performance, and compelling innovation. Our products include professional power tools and accessories, outdoor power equipment, and floor care. Our brands include Milwaukee®, AEG®, Ryobi®, Oreck®, Hoover®, Dirt Devil® and Vax®.

In this dynamic role, you will play a critical part in driving market share growth and maintaining TTI’s premier product lines within The Home Depot—our most valued and influential retail partner. You’ll be at the forefront of retail strategy execution, gaining hands-on experience in merchandising, sales analytics, and customer engagement. This position offers a unique opportunity to build a strong foundation in our core business operations while accelerating your career in a fast-paced, results-driven, and highly rewarding environment. • Plan and execute promotional events, product demos, and store walks to drive consumer engagement and increase product sell-through

• Support and implement strategic corporate brand marketing initiatives and promotional activities to increase brand awareness and drive sell-through

• Ensure brand presence and sales-readiness through strategic merchandising, optimal product placement, and completion of store objectives and resets—leveraging data analytics through Microsoft Power BI to drive decisions and maximize impact

• Develop a strong understanding of the retail marketplace, including customer profiles, product applications, competitive landscape, and channel dynamics

• Participate in TTI’s world class training program to be equipped with the knowledge to work independently within your assigned market

• Build and manage relationships with The Home Depot team members to enhance in-store execution and cultivate long-term business partnerships

• Effectively manage inventory levels through down-stocking, maintaining product accessibility, and ensure prompt reporting of all tasks and responsibilities

• Participate in merchandising resets to support TTI’s relentless innovation, ensuring the timely placement of cutting-edge products and solutions that drive growth, competitive advantage, and meet evolving market needs, all while adhering to TTI’s safety protocols

title: Sr. Electrical Engineer 1
description:
Job Description:

TTI has an opening in its Anderson, SC office for a Sr. Electrical Engineer 1. We offer competitive wages and a comprehensive benefits package -- tuition assistance, 401(k), medical/dental/vision coverage, vacation and holidays.

Primary Job Function

Our engineers are empowered to contribute to the full design of the electronics in our power tools, lithium-ion battery packs, and battery chargers. They have ownership in the development of design input documents, design of circuit schematics and PCB layouts, component selection and generation of BOMs, ordering parts, assembling and testing prototypes, firmware development, firmware testing, bench testing, writing design and test specs, supporting design verification testing prior to production, communicating with and supporting mass production.

The engineer will work closely with colleagues from other departments to define expectations of product functionality and ensure that the delivered product meets all aspects of the customer's requested specifications.

The candidate must have a can-do attitude, be willing to learn new technical skills, and be functional in both hardware and firmware. An ideal candidate would be comfortable in hands-on situations (e.g., PBCA rework, measurement equipment) and also be able approach problems from a theoretical perspective (e.g., simulation and calculations). Strong time-management skills and a production-focused mindset are required traits. Experience with power tools and home improvement / hobby work is a major plus.

Benefits:

• Full ownership of new projects; sense of accomplishment when "your" product is on store shelves

• Will work in a small group of electrical & embedded engineers (<15) with a collegial atmosphere

• Interact with component manufacturers to keep informed of new technologies and even help influence their direction

• We strive for constant improvement, both in our design processes and in employees' technical skills: At-work training (e.g., lunch & learns) is encouraged, and offsite trainings are typically available on a semi-annual basis.

• Opportunities for advancement in technical and managerial directions

• Excellent support for test equipment and materials needed to do our work

• Many opportunities are available, allowing engineers to grow and find a place on our team

• Great new facility: campus has on-site gym (free), cafeteria, outside acres to walk, jog and bike (mapped woods trail!), and participation in team-building extracurricular activities

Required Job Qualifications (Be ready to demonstrate and discuss examples):

• Minimum BS Electrical Engineering, BS Computer Engineering, or equivalent degree

• At least 5 years of relevant work experience

• Able to solve fundamental EE design circuits with ease (e.g., linear circuit analysis, determine function of small transistor circuits, op-amp design)

• Experience with LV (<40V) and MV (<100V) power electronics design -- MOSFETS, gate drives

• Proficiency with Printed Circuit Board layout and development tools, (e.g., Eagle, OrCAD, Altium)

• Able to set up and performing tests on hardware with test and measurement equipment -- oscilloscopes, multimeter, power supplies, etc.

• Familiarity and desire to do microcontroller firmware development in C

• Experience in prototyping and modifying circuits on dense PCB using SMT components

• Proficiency with SPICE modeling software such as LTSpice, Multisim, etc

• Comfortable and capable of explaining technical issues to technical and non-technical audiences in email, via powerpoint, and in meetings

• Able to travel to Asia as necessary: 0-5%

Prefer:

• Familiarity with Li-Ion battery management techniques, BLDC control, or flyback charger design is a big plus.

• Thermal simulation and modelling for electronic components experience is a big plus

• Significant experience in embedded C, such as in the creation of "platform" firmware or experience working on larger FW projects within a team (e.g., use of flowcharts and other planning documents, good grasp of GIT or other VCS)

• Experience with 8-bit and 32-bit MCUs (e.g., Atmel, TI, Microchip, NXP, ST Micro, ARM M0/M0+)

• Experience with IAR embedded workbench and similar IDEs for firmware development

• Familiarity with UL, IEC, EN, IEEE, or FCC standards for circuits, PCBs, and consumer electronics

• LabVIEW experience is a plus

title: Mold Maker I
description:
CKV Mold Maker I
Job Description:

Your Role on Our Team

At Milwaukee Tool, we are committed to delivering high-quality, innovative solutions to our users. The Mold Maker I is responsible for the maintenance, repair, troubleshooting, and improvement of production molds, tooling, and related equipment used in manufacturing operations. This entry-level, skilled trades position supports production by performing preventative maintenance, diagnosing tooling issues, conducting repairs, and assisting with mold changeovers while maintaining safety, quality, and productivity standards.

You’ll be DISRUPTIVE through these duties and responsibilities

• Consistently demonstrates safety first mindset; follows all safety related processes and procedures, quickly escalates safety related concerns or issues to create a safe work environment for all employees.

• Maintain work area, including but not limited to, mold storage, secondary equipment storage and mold crib, per 6s facility standards without direction.

• Perform routine preventive maintenance on molds, dies, tooling, and related equipment.

• Disassemble, inspect, clean, repair, and reassemble molds according to maintenance schedules and production requirements.

• Troubleshoot mold and tooling issues to identify root causes and implement corrective actions.

• Perform emergency mold repairs to minimize downtime and support production continuity.

• Repair mold components through machining, grinding, polishing, fitting, welding, and bench work activities.

• Assist in mold changeovers, setup verification, and startup activities.

• Operate machine shop equipment including lathes, milling machines, surface grinders, drill presses, and other precision equipment.

• Utilize hand tools, measuring instruments, and precision inspection equipment to manufacture or repair mold components.

• Maintain dimensional accuracy using metric and standard measurement systems.

• Perform TIG welding and other approved repair processes when required.

• Verify repaired and manufactured mold components meet specifications and quality standards.

• Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, productivity, cost reduction, and equipment reliability.

• Identify opportunities to improve mold performance and reduce recurring equipment failures.

• Assist in documenting repairs, modifications, and maintenance activities.

• Collaborate with production, engineering, maintenance, and quality teams to resolve tooling issues.

• Communicate equipment concerns and repair status effectively.

• Support production schedules by responding promptly to tooling-related issues.

• Work unsupervised while using manual and/or power equipment and tools while performing multiple tasks.

• Proactively work with team members to meet the needs of the production floor.

• Ability to work overtime with advanced or little notice.

• All other duties as assigned.

description:
Job Description:

About Us:

TTI (Techtronic Industries) is a fast-paced, high energy, organization that rewards out-of-the-box thinking to foster innovation allowing us to be the best in our industry. We provide a multi-faceted training program and hands-on field experience that will stimulate, challenge, and reward you.

TTI is a world-class leader in design, manufacturing and marketing of power tools and accessories, outdoor product equipment, and floor care products. Our consumers range from professional and industrial users in the home improvement, repair, and construction industries to homeowners & DIY enthusiasts. Our unrelenting strategic focus on powerful brands, innovative products, operational excellence, and exceptional people drives our culture. This focus and drive provide TTI with a powerful platform for sustainable leadership and strong growth.

Our brands and products are recognized worldwide for their deep heritage, superior quality, outstanding performance, and compelling innovation. Our products include professional power tools and accessories, outdoor power equipment, and floor care. Our brands include Milwaukee®, AEG®, Ryobi®, Oreck®, Hoover®, Dirt Devil® and Vax®.

In this dynamic role, you will play a critical part in driving market share growth and maintaining TTI’s premier product lines within The Home Depot—our most valued and influential retail partner. You’ll be at the forefront of retail strategy execution, gaining hands-on experience in merchandising, sales analytics, and customer engagement. This position offers a unique opportunity to build a strong foundation in our core business operations while accelerating your career in a fast-paced, results-driven, and highly rewarding environment. Your contributions will directly impact TTI’s presence in the retail space, positioning you for continued advancement within the organization.

Duties and Responsibilities:

• Exceed sales targets by delivering best-in-class Business to Consumer sales and customer service within The Home Depot, engaging directly with customers to understand their needs and recommend tailored TTI product solutions, all while demonstrating deep product knowledge and enthusiasm

• Plan and execute promotional events, product demos, and store walks to drive consumer engagement and increase product sell-through

• Support and implement strategic corporate brand marketing initiatives and promotional activities to increase brand awareness and drive sell-through

• Ensure brand presence and sales-readiness through strategic merchandising, optimal product placement, and completion of store objectives and resets—leveraging data analytics through Microsoft Power BI to drive decisions and maximize impact

• Develop a strong understanding of the retail marketplace, including customer profiles, product applications, competitive landscape, and channel dynamics

• Participate in TTI’s world class training program to be equipped with the knowledge to work independently within your assigned market

• Build and manage relationships with The Home Depot team members to enhance in-store execution and cultivate long-term business partnerships

• Effectively manage inventory levels through down-stocking, maintaining product accessibility, and ensure prompt reporting of all tasks and responsibilities

• Participate in merchandising resets to support TTI’s relentless innovation, ensuring the timely placement of cutting-edge products and solutions that drive growth, competitive advantage, and meet evolving market needs, all while adhering to TTI’s safety protocols

Note: Employee's duties and responsibilities are not limited by the above. Other duties may be assigned as deemed necessary by the employee's supervisor. In addition to the basic requirements of the position, all employees are expected to meet the company's goals of continual improvement in the areas of knowledge, skills, processes, and quality.

Job / Employment Requirements:

• Must be at least 21 years of age or older

• Eligible to work in the United States without sponsorship or restrictions

• Ability to pass drug screening and Motor Vehicle Report screening

• Must have a valid United States driver’s license for at least one continuous full year in one state

• Must have a personal vehicle / reliable form of transportation

• Possess and maintain valid personal vehicle insurance listing you as the primary driver

• Position requires travel to/ from assigned store location(s) as well as occasional travel for meetings, projects, events, etc. Air travel will be required

• Employees will also be required to transport a small amount of company property (company devices, demo tools, tool kit, safety supplies)

• Capable of reaching and/or lifting overhead in addition to ascending/descending ladders to move product.

• Capable of lifting and transporting heavy tools (up to 50 lbs.) and requesting assistance as needed

• Capable of using hands to maneuver small objects, assemble tools and build displays

• Ability to work nights and weekends – weekends will be required at different points throughout the year

• Ability to work in a retail environment full time and stand for the duration of the shift, with the exception of meal and rest breaks

• Applicant should be self-motivated and a team player with strong organizational, planning and time management skills.

• The applicant must be MS Office proficient

• Multilingual abilities preferred in specific markets depending on business needs

• Formal higher education preferred but not required – Equivalent experience will be considered

• Relocation may be required for future promotional opportunities

Compensation and Benefits:

• Sales Contests and Incentives to Earn Additional Income (In Correlation with Business Needs/ Focuses)

• Company iPhone and iPad

title: Sr Supplier Quality Engineer
description:
Job Description:

The Senior Supplier Quality Engineer is a technical and cross-functional leader responsible for critical suppliers, complex supplier quality issues, and major improvement initiatives. This role applies strong manufacturing, quality-system, problem-solving, and project leadership capability to reduce supplier risk, strengthen supplier performance, and ensure readiness for new product development, transfers, and ongoing production. The Senior SQE operates independently, influences decisions across multiple functions, coaches less-experienced engineers, and drives accountability with suppliers and internal stakeholders.

The role partners closely with Engineering, Advanced Quality, Purchasing, Operations, Manufacturing, and global quality teams to translate technical and business requirements into supplier quality plans, qualification activities, process controls, corrective actions, and measurable performance improvements. It is expected to identify risk early, communicate clearly, and lead difficult supplier situations to sustainable resolution.

You'll be DISRUPTIVE through these duties and responsibilities:

• Lead supplier quality improvement roadmaps that address chronic quality issues, escapes, process capability, control effectiveness, and supplier execution.

• Partner with suppliers to strengthen process capability, quality systems, inspection methods, measurement systems, manufacturing controls, and continuous improvement practices.

• Lead cross-functional teams and major supplier-quality initiatives, establish clear deliverables and critical paths, and hold stakeholders accountable for timely execution.

• Use supplier performance data, trends, and KPIs to identify systemic risk, prioritize intervention, and communicate clear recovery plans and decision points.

• Influence sourcing, engineering, operations, and supplier decisions through fact-based risk assessment, technical judgment, and practical understanding of quality, delivery, cost, and schedule trade-offs.

• Own supplier quality performance for assigned critical or high-risk suppliers, commodities, and projects; establish priorities and drive actions to closure.

• Lead supplier qualification, assessment, onboarding, and surveillance activities, including complex process and quality-system audits.

• Lead Supplier Quality engagement through New Product Development and product/process transfers, using VIGOR and applicable qualification requirements to identify manufacturing risk, validate readiness, and protect project timing.

• Develop and execute supplier and part qualification plans, including manufacturing feasibility, process risk assessment, control plans, capability studies, measurement strategy, FAI/SIR and applicable GPAP, GECKO, and/or SER deliverables.

• Lead critical supplier escalations, containment, root cause investigation, 8D/SCAR corrective action, effectiveness verification, and prevention of recurrence.

• Solve complex supplier quality and manufacturing problems using data, structured problem solving, statistical methods, technical drawings/specifications, GD&T, metrology, and appropriate process expertise.

• Coach and mentor SQEs and engineers; share technical knowledge, review problem-solving and qualification work, and help build capability across the Supplier Quality team.

• Improve Supplier Quality standard work, methods, dashboards, and tools by identifying recurring gaps and introducing practical improvements that increase visibility, consistency, and prevention.

• Communicate complex technical issues clearly to suppliers and internal leaders, including concise risk statements, recommendations, escalation needs, and recovery status.

• Manage multiple complex priorities in a fast-paced environment and travel to supplier and company locations as business needs require.

What TOOLS you'll bring with you:

• Bachelor's degree in Quality, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field.

• 5-8 years of progressive experience in Supplier Quality, manufacturing quality, engineering, operations, or a related technical discipline.

• Demonstrated ability to independently manage critical suppliers and lead complex cross-functional supplier quality improvements and escalations.

• Strong working knowledge of supplier auditing, supplier selection and qualification, corrective action, quality systems, manufacturing process controls, and supplier performance management.

• Demonstrated proficiency in New Product Development and supplier/part qualification, including manufacturing feasibility, process capability, risk assessment, control plans, and applicable Part Approval requirements.

• Demonstrated ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, GD&T, inspection requirements, and measurement methods and translate requirements into supplier controls.

• Experience leading structured problem solving and data analysis for complex issues using methods such as root cause analysis, 8D, statistical analysis, and process capability evaluation.

• Ability to lead projects and cross-functional teams, influence without direct authority, negotiate resolution of difficult issues, and drive accountability across suppliers and stakeholders.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to tailor technical content to engineers, suppliers, operations teams, sourcing partners, and leadership.

• Working knowledge of quality and business systems used to manage supplier performance, project execution, documentation, and data analysis.

• Practical manufacturing-process depth in one or more relevant areas such as electronics/mechatronics, molding, casting, machining, stamping/forming, heat treatment, coatings, assembly, motors, welding, or metrology.

• Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to 10-25% depending on business needs

Other TOOLS we prefer you to have:

• Lead Auditor training and experience with ISO 9001, IATF 16949/TS 16949, VDA 6.3, or comparable quality-system/process auditing.

• Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma training/certification and demonstrated application of continuous-improvement methods with suppliers.

• Professional quality certification such as ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or equivalent.

• Experience with complex electromechanical products, high-volume manufacturing, multi-tier/global suppliers, or regulated product requirements.

• Experience using Minitab, Power BI, or comparable analytical tools to identify trends, quantify risk, and communicate supplier performance.

Milwaukee Tool is an equal opportunity employer.
